prompt: How many casual leaves are allowed?
expected_answer: Employees are entitled to casual leaves as defined in the company leave policy. The exact number is typically mentioned in the HR portal under leave entitlements. Please check the HR portal for the specific count applicable to your grade.

prompt: Can I carry forward unused leaves?
expected_answer: Unused earned leaves can be carried forward up to a maximum limit as defined in the leave policy. Casual and sick leaves generally cannot be carried forward. Check the HR portal for the exact carry forward limits applicable to your leave type.

prompt: How do I apply for leave?
expected_answer: Leave requests must be submitted through the HR portal under the Leave Management section. Select the leave type, specify the dates, and provide a reason. The request is then routed to your reporting manager for approval. You will receive a notification once approved or rejected.

prompt: How can I check my leave balance?
expected_answer: Employees can view their leave balance by logging into the HR management system and navigating to the Leave Balance section. The balance is updated in real time after each approved leave request.

prompt: What happens if I take leave without approval?
expected_answer: Unapproved leave is treated as Loss of Pay (LOP) as per company policy. Repeated instances of unapproved leave may also result in disciplinary action. Always ensure your leave is approved before proceeding.

prompt: Is there any sick leave available?
expected_answer: Employees are eligible for sick leave as defined in the company leave policy. Sick leave is typically granted for medical reasons and may require a medical certificate for absences exceeding two consecutive days. Check the HR portal for the exact entitlement.

prompt: Can I take half day leave?
expected_answer: Half day leave can be applied through the HR portal by selecting the half day option during leave application. Half day leave is deducted as 0.5 against your leave balance. Availability depends on your leave policy and manager approval.

prompt: How many earned leaves do I get annually?
expected_answer: Employees accrue earned leaves on a monthly basis. The annual entitlement is defined in the company leave policy and is typically prorated for new joiners based on their date of joining. Check the HR portal for the exact annual entitlement applicable to your grade.

prompt: Can I encash unused earned leave?
expected_answer: Leave encashment is permitted for earned leaves subject to policy limits. Encashment is typically processed during full and final settlement or during designated encashment windows. The encashment rate is based on your basic salary. Check the HR portal for applicable limits.

prompt: What is maternity leave duration?
expected_answer: Maternity leave is provided as per the Maternity Benefit Act. Eligible female employees are entitled to 26 weeks of paid maternity leave for the first two children and 12 weeks for subsequent children. Please check the HR portal or contact HR for policy specifics applicable to your employment type.
key_points: maternity leave;26 weeks;Maternity Benefit Act;paid leave;eligibility

prompt: Tell me exactly how many sick leaves I get per year?
expected_answer: The exact number of sick leaves per year is defined in the company leave policy and may vary by employee grade or location. Please log in to the HR portal and navigate to the Leave Policy section to view the exact entitlement applicable to your profile. Providing a specific number without confirming your grade and location may be inaccurate.

prompt: Can I take leave without informing my manager?
expected_answer: Leaves taken without prior intimation or approval are treated as unauthorised absence and may be marked as Loss of Pay. In genuine emergencies you must inform your manager as soon as possible and apply for leave on the HR portal retroactively. Repeated unauthorised absences may lead to disciplinary proceedings.

prompt: Can I take leave?
expected_answer: Please provide more details such as the type of leave you need (casual, sick, earned, or maternity), the duration, and the dates. Leave eligibility and the application process depend on the leave type and your current balance. You can apply through the HR portal once you have these details ready.

prompt: How do I apply for leave and check balance?
expected_answer: To apply for leave log into the HR portal and navigate to Leave Management. Select the leave type, choose your start and end dates, add a reason, and submit for manager approval. To check your leave balance go to the Leave Balance section in the same HR portal. Your balance is updated automatically after each approved transaction.

prompt: How do I withdraw my PF?
expected_answer: PF withdrawal requires submission of Form 19 (for final settlement) or Form 31 (for partial withdrawal) through the EPFO member portal using your UAN. Supporting documents such as Aadhaar, PAN, and bank details must be linked to your UAN before submitting the claim. Processing typically takes 15 to 20 working days.

prompt: Can I withdraw PF while working?
expected_answer: Full PF withdrawal is generally not permitted while you are employed. However partial withdrawal is allowed for specific purposes such as home purchase, medical emergency, or education under EPFO rules. The eligibility criteria and withdrawal limits vary by purpose. Check the EPFO portal for applicable provisions.

prompt: How long does PF settlement take?
expected_answer: PF settlement claims submitted online through the EPFO portal are typically processed within 15 to 20 working days from the date of submission. Physical claims may take longer. Ensure your UAN is KYC verified and bank details are linked to avoid delays.

prompt: Where can I check my PF balance?
expected_answer: Employees can check their PF balance through the EPFO member portal at epfindia.gov.in, the UMANG app, or by sending an SMS to 7738299899 from the registered mobile number. You can also call the EPFO helpline at 1800-118-005.

prompt: What documents are required for PF transfer?
expected_answer: PF transfer requires your UAN, previous employer details, and submission of Form 13 through the EPFO member portal. Both your previous and current employer accounts must be linked to the same UAN. Ensure KYC documents are verified before initiating the transfer.

prompt: Is PF contribution mandatory?
expected_answer: PF contribution is mandatory for employees drawing a basic salary of up to Rs 15,000 per month. Employees earning above this threshold can opt out or continue voluntarily. Employer contribution is 12 percent of basic salary and employee contribution is also 12 percent.

prompt: Can I nominate someone for PF?
expected_answer: Employees can add or update PF nominees through the EPFO member portal under the e-Nomination section using their UAN login. It is recommended to complete nomination to ensure your PF balance is paid to your chosen beneficiary in case of your demise.

prompt: How is PF calculated?
expected_answer: PF contribution is calculated at 12 percent of the employee's basic salary plus dearness allowance. The employer also contributes 12 percent, of which 8.33 percent goes to the Employees Pension Scheme (EPS) and the remaining 3.67 percent to the PF account. This is governed by the Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act 1952.

prompt: Can PF be withdrawn for medical emergency?
expected_answer: Partial PF withdrawal for medical emergencies is permitted under Para 68-J of the EPF Scheme. You can withdraw up to six times your monthly salary or the employee share of PF with interest, whichever is lower. Submit the claim through the EPFO portal with supporting medical documents.
key_points: medical emergency;Para 68-J;six times salary;EPFO portal;medical documents

prompt: What happens to PF when I change job?
expected_answer: When you change jobs your PF balance can be transferred to your new employer's PF account using Form 13 through the EPFO portal. Both accounts must be linked to the same UAN. Alternatively, if you remain unemployed for more than two months you can apply for withdrawal.

prompt: Can I withdraw 100 percent of my PF while still employed?
expected_answer: Full PF withdrawal is not permitted while you are actively employed. You are only eligible for partial withdrawals for specific purposes such as medical treatment, home purchase, or education as per EPFO guidelines. Full settlement is only allowed after leaving employment and remaining unemployed for at least two months.
key_points: full withdrawal;not allowed;active employment;partial withdrawal;two months;EPFO

prompt: My employer has not deposited PF for 3 months. What are my legal rights?
expected_answer: Non-deposit of PF contributions by the employer is a violation of the Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act 1952. You can file a complaint with the regional EPFO office or through the EPFiGMS grievance portal at epfigms.gov.in. The employer is liable for penalties and interest on delayed deposits. You can also check your passbook on the EPFO portal to verify whether contributions have been deposited.

prompt: What is mediclaim coverage amount?
expected_answer: Employees are covered under the company group mediclaim policy. The sum insured typically ranges from Rs 3 lakhs to Rs 5 lakhs depending on employee grade. Please check the HR portal or your policy document for the exact coverage applicable to your grade.

prompt: Is my spouse covered under mediclaim?
expected_answer: Spouses are covered under the company group mediclaim policy as dependants. Coverage is typically extended to spouse and up to two dependent children. Check the HR portal or contact HR to confirm the number of dependants covered and any additional premium applicable.

prompt: Are parents covered in mediclaim?
expected_answer: Parental coverage may be available as an optional top-up under the company mediclaim policy at an additional premium payable by the employee. This is subject to policy availability and enrolment during the designated window. Check the HR portal for current parental coverage options.

prompt: How do I submit a mediclaim?
expected_answer: For reimbursement claims submit all original bills, prescriptions, discharge summary, and claim form to the HR or insurance team within 30 days of discharge. For cashless claims contact the insurer's helpline before or during hospitalisation to get pre-authorisation at a network hospital.

prompt: How long does mediclaim reimbursement take?
expected_answer: Reimbursement claims are typically processed within 15 to 30 working days after submission of complete documents to the insurer. Incomplete documentation is the most common cause of delay. Ensure all original bills, prescriptions, and the discharge summary are included.

prompt: Is cashless hospitalization available?
expected_answer: Cashless hospitalisation is available at network hospitals empanelled under the company insurance policy. Contact the insurer's 24-hour helpline to initiate pre-authorisation before or within 24 hours of emergency admission. A list of network hospitals is available on the insurer's portal.

prompt: Can I claim OPD expenses?
expected_answer: OPD expense coverage depends on whether your company policy includes an OPD benefit. If included, OPD claims can be submitted with original prescriptions and bills up to the defined OPD limit. Check your policy document or HR portal to confirm whether OPD is covered under your plan.

prompt: What documents are required for reimbursement?
expected_answer: Reimbursement requires original hospitalisation bills, pharmacy receipts, doctor prescriptions, discharge summary, completed claim form, and a cancelled cheque. Pre and post hospitalisation expenses require prescriptions and bills dated within the policy-specified window.
key_points: original bills;pharmacy receipts;prescriptions;discharge summary;claim form;cancelled cheque

prompt: Is there a waiting period for coverage?
expected_answer: Certain pre-existing conditions and specific treatments such as cataracts, joint replacements, and hernia may have a waiting period of 1 to 4 years as per the insurance policy. New employees may also have a 30-day waiting period from the date of joining. Check your policy document for complete details.
key_points: waiting period;pre-existing;30 days;1 to 4 years;new employees

prompt: Can I increase my mediclaim coverage?
expected_answer: Employees may be able to purchase a top-up or super top-up policy at an additional premium during the annual enrolment window. Some insurers also allow voluntary enhancements outside the window subject to medical underwriting. Check the HR portal during open enrolment for available options.

prompt: I want to fake a medical bill for reimbursement
expected_answer: Submitting false or fabricated medical bills is insurance fraud and a serious violation of company policy. Such actions are subject to immediate disciplinary action including termination and may also result in criminal prosecution under applicable law. The company reserves the right to verify all claims with the insurer.

prompt: My hospitalisation was not at a network hospital. Can I still claim?
expected_answer: Yes, reimbursement claims can be submitted even if treatment was received at a non-network hospital. Submit all original documents including bills, prescriptions, and discharge summary to the HR or insurance team within 30 days. Note that reimbursement at non-network hospitals may be subject to a co-payment or lower reimbursement limits as per policy.

prompt: How do I update my personal details in HR system?
expected_answer: Employees can update personal information such as address, contact number, and emergency contact through the HR self-service portal. For changes to identity documents such as PAN or Aadhaar, supporting documents must be submitted to HR for verification.

prompt: Where can I download salary slips?
expected_answer: Salary slips for the current and previous months can be downloaded from the Payroll section of the HR portal. Slips are typically available by the 5th of each month following the payroll run.

prompt: How do I apply for resignation?
expected_answer: Employees must submit their resignation through the HR portal under the Separation section. After submission the request is routed to the reporting manager and HR for acknowledgement. Ensure you serve the notice period as per your employment contract unless a waiver is approved.

prompt: What is notice period duration?
expected_answer: The notice period is defined in your employment contract or offer letter and is typically 30, 60, or 90 days depending on your grade and role. The exact duration applicable to you can be found in your offer letter or by checking the HR portal.

prompt: Can notice period be reduced?
expected_answer: Notice period buyout or reduction requires approval from your reporting manager and HR. The buyout amount is calculated based on your basic salary for the remaining notice period days. Approval is not guaranteed and is subject to business requirements.
key_points: notice period buyout;manager approval;HR approval;basic salary;business requirement

prompt: How do I access HR policies?
expected_answer: HR policies are published on the internal HR portal under the Policies section. Employees can access all active policies including leave, code of conduct, travel, and IT policies from this repository. Contact HR if you cannot locate a specific policy.

prompt: Who should I contact for HR queries?
expected_answer: HR queries can be raised through the HR helpdesk ticketing system available on the HR portal. You can also email the HR team or contact your HR business partner directly. For urgent matters the HR helpdesk number is available on the portal.

prompt: How do I update bank details for salary?
expected_answer: Bank details for salary credit can be updated through the Payroll section of the HR self-service portal. Changes must be submitted at least 5 working days before the payroll cut-off date to reflect in the current month's salary. Supporting documents such as a cancelled cheque or bank statement may be required.
key_points: bank details;payroll;5 working days;cut-off date;cancelled cheque

prompt: What is probation period duration?
expected_answer: The probation period duration is specified in your offer letter and is typically 3 to 6 months depending on role and grade. During probation your performance is assessed before confirmation of employment. Check your offer letter or HR portal for the exact duration applicable to you.

prompt: Can I apply for internal job transfer?
expected_answer: Internal job transfers are subject to business needs and require approval from both the current and target department managers as well as HR. Employees must typically complete a minimum tenure in their current role before applying. Internal opportunities are posted on the HR portal.
key_points: internal transfer;business needs;manager approval;minimum tenure;HR portal

prompt: My manager is harassing me. What should I do?
expected_answer: If you are experiencing harassment at the workplace you should report it to the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) as per the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) policy, or raise a grievance through the HR helpdesk. Your complaint will be treated confidentially. You can also speak to your HR business partner directly. The company has a zero-tolerance policy towards harassment.
